Subject: Dedicated throughput guarantees — clarifications

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our engineering leadership asked for a precise definition of the throughput guarantees Redwood would provide for a Dedicated pool: specifically tokens/sec and requests/sec at a pinned model, plus how you measure latency (end-to-end vs. generation). We also need an explanation of GPU pool sizing assumptions that map a reserved commit to the promised throughput.

Key asks from Acorn:
- A clear tokens/sec and requests/sec SLA, documented per model family and sequence length.
- Expected p50/p95 latencies for 32/128 token responses.
- Measurement methodology for reporting uptime/throughput: window, agents, warm caches, and exclusion rules.
- How burst capacity works and whether queueing/backpressure could affect p95.

We have a preferred target: support 75 reqs/sec with median reply size ~64 tokens for peak clinical-use bursts. Please advise on what reserved commit we should plan for and what discount tiers make sense for a 12-month commit.

Attaching our sample traffic profile.

—Emma

High level answer up front: we can commit to both tokens/sec and requests/sec guarantees for a pinned model/version on Dedicated, with SLAs specified as a 72-hour rolling window (informal draft below). Final numbers depend on the model and sequence-length distribution, so please confirm the model family you plan to run in production.

Draft SLA summary (placeholders until model is pinned):
- Throughput guarantee: 30k tokens/sec sustained (72-hour rolling), equivalent to ~75 requests/sec at 64 tokens/response.
- Requests/sec guarantee: 80 reqs/sec sustained (72-hour rolling), measured with 95th percentile per-request steady-state latency target.
- Latency targets (p95) for pinned model: <= 450ms for 32-token responses, <= 900ms for 128-token responses (end-to-end, excludes network across customer edge).

We can size a Dedicated pool and map commits to GPU counts; Rishi will propose pricing/discount tiers for a 12-month commit. Vivek — can you post the measurement methodology and a recommended stress test config?

Thanks,
Lauren

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.example, rishi_malhotra@redwood.example, monica_patel@redwood.example
Cc: Emma Jones <emma.jones@acorn.health>
Date: 2026-02-11T10:24:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated throughput guarantees — clarifications

Folks — adding the technical detail and an attached test plan (dedicated_throughput_testplan.md). Key points below.

Assumptions and baseline mapping:
- Model: we tested on a medium/large open model family comparable to Llama-2 13B quantized; numbers will change for larger or sparsely activated models. Please confirm exact model/version.
- GPU options: typical Dedicated pools use H100 or A100 class instances. Our baseline mapping: 1 x H100 (full node) => ~12k-18k tokens/sec for 512-seq mixing; 1 x A100 80GB => ~8k-12k tokens/sec depending on quantization and kernel path.
- For your target (75 req/s at ~64 tokens), we expect ~30k tokens/sec sustained requirement. That maps to roughly 3 x H100 or 4 x A100s with conservative headroom (20% buffer) for KV cache pressure and multi-tenant burst behavior.

Measurement methodology (summary):
1) Test harness: we run a dedicated benchmark agent in the same region (us-west-2) generating client-like traffic against the pinned model binary.
2) Warm-up: 30 minutes of gradual ramp to hydrate KV cache and fill kernel JIT paths. Measurements exclude the warm-up window.
3) Steady-state window: 72-hour rolling window; sustained throughput is measured over 1-minute buckets and SLA computed as the 72-hour median of per-minute throughput (we also report the 95th percentile of per-minute latency).
4) Tokens/sec measurement: count of generated tokens server-side (post-decoding) aggregated per second; request size normalization uses standardized 32/64/128 token bins for SLA mapping.
5) Requests/sec measurement: completed requests per second where each request meets minimum latency threshold (no artificially long-running items).
6) Latency: end-to-end request latency measured from ingress to final token emit, reported at p50/p95/p99. Network egress to customer edge is excluded, but we can run e2e tests if Acorn provides an IP to test from.
7) Exclusions & incident handling: planned maintenance, prolonged cold starts (first 30 minutes post-deploy) and third-party cloud interruptions are excluded from SLA windows; we provide a public incident log for transparency.

Burst behavior & queueing:
- Dedicated pools support configured burst capacity (short lived) using pre-warmed spare GPUs. Burst is an add-on; if enabled, bursts are guaranteed for X minutes per hour. Without burst add-on, excess requests are queued — p95 may degrade under extreme overcommit; we set throttles and backpressure rather than silently dropping.

Acceptance test & runbook:
- We propose a staged acceptance: 1) lab run (our agents only), 2) joint-run with Acorn traffic profile (attached), 3) 72-hour observation before final go-live. The attached md has the exact cURL/locust/test-agent commands.

I attached dedicated_throughput_testplan.md and the sample traffic profile they sent. Happy to jump on a call to walk through the script.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: dedicated_throughput_testplan.md]

- Recommended reserved commit: Equivalent of 4 x A100-80GB (or 3 x H100) for predictable throughput matching the 30k tokens/sec target.
- Pricing: we can offer a 15% discount on list Dedicated unit rates for a 12-month commit at that scale. 20% available at 24-months or if you add our burst add-on.
- Credits: if measured throughput over a billing month falls below 95% of guaranteed tokens/sec (per the 72-hour rolling measurement), we will issue service credits pro rata. Credits are capped per contract.
- Onboarding: 2-week joint acceptance test included, additional engineering hours billed at T&M unless you buy the onboarding package (standard for Enterprise).
